extracted.intended_audience: current and prospective patent and trademark practitioners; inventors seeking representation before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on who may represent clients before the USPTO and the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's roles, including registration requirements, disciplinary oversight, and resources for finding practitioners. Covers patent practitioner registration, trademark practitioner eligibility, and OED programs and notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered patent practitioner eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered patent practitioners are individuals who have passed the USPTO's registration exam and met the qualifications to represent patent applicants before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED administers the registration exam and maintains a roster of current patent practitioners. See 'Becoming a patent practitioner' for application, requirements, forms, and exam information; consult 'Registration exam update' and related notices for current procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark practitioner eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark practitioners are attorneys who are active members in good standing of the bar of the highest court of any State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Becoming a trademark practitioner' for more information about the requirements to represent others in trademark matters before the USPTO and 'Finding a trademark practitioner' for locating attorneys who practice trademark law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining eligibility / roster and public notices
rubrics_metrics.description: OED maintains a roster of current patent practitioners and publishes notices such as 'Registration to practice notices', 'Federal Register notices', and 'Official Gazette notices'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners and the public should consult the roster and OED notices to verify registration status and monitor official announcements related to registration and practitioner eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary oversight and grievances
rubrics_metrics.description: OED investigates grievances submitted against practitioners and provides public information about disciplinary actions against practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must adhere to ethics rules; the OED handles investigations and publishes disciplinary information. See 'Information for current practitioners' for ethics rules and related forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to representation resources (finding practitioners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn how to find registered patent agents and attorneys who are eligible to practice before the USPTO in patent matters and how to find attorneys who practice trademark law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the USPTO-provided search tools, the OED roster, and published notices to locate eligible representatives. Inventors seeking help may also explore the Patent Pro Bono Program coordinated by OED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Pro Bono and Law School Clinic programs
rubrics_metrics.description: OED coordinates a nationwide Patent Pro Bono Program for under-resourced inventors seeking free legal help and administers a Law School Clinic Certification Program where law students gain experience in intellectual property law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under-resourced inventors can apply for pro bono assistance; law schools may participate in the clinic certification program to provide supervised student representation experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information and resources for current practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Find useful information for current patent and trademark practitioners including ethics rules, common forms, and online access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should consult these resources to maintain compliance, access common forms, and stay informed of OED guidance and procedural updates.
